title: Boss: capacity and failure
summary: A scheduler, an OOM detector and a scaling planner.

steps.title: The scene
body: Black Friday is coming. You need to know where new pods would land, which pods are dying of memory, and how far the HPA would scale. Build the tools.
The scheduler's core is simple: **filter** nodes that can fit the pod's requests (free = allocatable âˆ’ sum of requests already placed), then **score** the survivors and pick the best.

steps.title: A tiny scheduler
prompt: Write `Dictionary<string, string> Schedule(List<(string Name, int CpuM, int MemMi)> pods, List<(string Name, int CpuM, int MemMi)> nodes)`.

For each pod **in order**: candidates are nodes whose free CPU and free memory are both at least the pod's requests. Pick the node with the **most free CPU** after placement (spreading); ties by node name. Map pod â†’ node name, or â†’ `"Pending"` if nothing fits. Placing a pod uses up its requests on that node.
starter: Dictionary<string, string> Schedule(List<(string Name, int CpuM, int MemMi)> pods, List<(string Name, int CpuM, int MemMi)> nodes)
solution: Dictionary<string, string> Schedule(List<(string Name, int CpuM, int MemMi)> pods, List<(string Name, int CpuM, int MemMi)> nodes)
var freeCpu = nodes.ToDictionary(n => n.Name, n => n.CpuM);
var freeMem = nodes.ToDictionary(n => n.Name, n => n.MemMi);
template: var dojoNodes = new List<(string Name, int CpuM, int MemMi)> { ("node-a", 2000, 4096), ("node-b", 1000, 8192) };
Dojo.Eq("api-1 to most free CPU", "node-a", dojoS["api-1"]);
Dojo.Eq("api-2 node-a still has the most free CPU", "node-a", dojoS["api-2"]);
Dojo.Eq("api-3 tie broken by name", "node-a", dojoS["api-3"]);
hints: Track free CPU and memory per node in two dictionaries.

steps.title: Find OOM victims
steps.prompt: Given lines of `kubectl get pods -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,REASON:.status.containerStatuses[0].lastState.terminated.reason,RESTARTS:.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount` (header first; `<none>` when there is no reason), write `List<string> OomVictims(string output, int minRestarts)` returning names whose `REASON` is `OOMKilled` and whose restarts are at least `minRestarts`, sorted by restarts descending, then name.
template:
var dojoOut = "NAME          REASON      RESTARTS
report-1      OOMKilled   12
api-1         <none>      0
api-2         Error       3
worker-a      OOMKilled   4
worker-b      OOMKilled   12
batch-z       OOMKilled   1";
Dojo.Eq("none", new List<string>(), OomVictims("NAME REASON RESTARTS\na <none> 0", 0));
hints: Split into columns like before; there are exactly three.
Sort with `OrderByDescending` on the parsed restarts, then `ThenBy` name.

steps.title: Will the HPA's pods fit?
prompt: Combine the HPA and capacity. Write `string Plan(int current, double cpuUtil, double target, int min, int max, int podCpuM, int clusterFreeCpuM)`:
- compute desired replicas exactly as in the HPA lesson (10% tolerance, ceil, clamp)
- `extra = desired - current`; if `extra <= 0` return `"scale to D"`
- pods that fit = `clusterFreeCpuM / podCpuM` (integer division). If all extra pods fit, return `"scale to D"`; otherwise `"scale to D, N Pending"` where N is how many will not fit.
starter: string Plan(int current, double cpuUtil, double target, int min, int max, int podCpuM, int clusterFreeCpuM)
solution: string Plan(int current, double cpuUtil, double target, int min, int max, int podCpuM, int clusterFreeCpuM)
return fit >= extra ? $"scale to {desired}" : $"scale to {desired}, {extra - fit} Pending";
template: Dojo.Eq("not enough room", "scale to 10, 3 Pending", Plan(5, 120, 60, 2, 10, 500, 1200));
hints: Integer division gives how many pods fit.
